title: Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of Encaleret in Participants With Chronic Hypoparathyroidism
official: A Phase 3, Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo Controlled, Parallel-Group Study With an Open-Label Extension Investigating Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of Encaleret in Participants With Chronic Hypoparathyroidism
summary: Main objective: To demonstrate the efficacy of encaleret compared with placebo treatment on blood calcium and 24-hour urinary calcium excretion
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1.  Participants aged ≥16 years  (or aged ≥18 years in the EU) at the time of signing the informed consent or assent must have had a clinically confirmed diagnosis of chronic HP, with disease duration of at least 26 weeks prior to screening. The cause of chronic HP can be postsurgical, autoimmune, genetic, or idiopathic. The diagnosis of chronic HP is confirmed by a documented history of hypocalcemia with inappropriately low serum PTH levels
2. 2. For participants with nonsurgical chronic HP etiology, sufficient documentation that a participant does not harbor any variants in CASR or GNA11 that are classified as  pathogenic, likely pathogenic, or of uncertain significance, with the exception of benign  common  polymorphisms (CASR A986S and R990G) is needed. Note: Sufficient documentation is defined as a copy of a prior genetic test result from a local laboratory. Note: In the absence of any sufficient documentation of prior genetic testing for CASR/GNA11 variants, participants with idiopathic HP must be willing to undergo CASR/GNA11 variant analysis. Similarly, participants with familial/genetic HP who do not have a genetic analysis report to demonstrate the underlying cause of their chronic HP  must be willing to undergo CASR/GNA11 variant analysis.
3. 3. Participants must be on stable doses of calcium and active vitamin D supplementation at or above the following minimum thresholds for at least 6 weeks prior to screening.For participants enrolled in study sites outside Japan: a. Calcitriol ≥0.5 μg/day or alfacalcidol ≥1.0 μg/day b. Elemental calcium ≥800 mg/day (eg, calcium citrate, calcium carbonate) For participants enrolled at study sites in Japan: a. Calcitriol ≥0.5 μg/day or alfacalcidol ≥1.0 μg/day For participants enrolled at study sites in Japan, the elemental calcium requirement during screening does not apply due to local clinical practice and dietary calcium intake patterns; however, participants must be willing to take elemental calcium supplements as  needed during the study in accordance with the protocol-specified titration algorithm. Note: As needed (PRN) doses of calcium and active vitamin D supplementation are not  counted toward the minimum dosing threshold.
4. 4. Participants must meet cCa and 24-hour UCa criteria during screening. If participants do not meet these criteria, see Section 4.1.1 for details regarding conventional therapy dose adjustments.
5. 5. Participants have serum 25(OH) vitamin D concentration of 20 to 80 ng/mL (50 to 200 nmol/L).
6. 6. Participants have serum magnesium concentration within the reference range.
7. 7. Participants must be capable of giving signed informed consent or assent, which includes compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the informed consent form and in this protocol.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1. Genetically confirmed diagnosis of autosomal dominant hypocalcemia type 1 or type 2 due to activating variants in CASR or GNA11, respectively.
2. 2. History of hypocalcemic seizure 3 months prior to screening.
3. 3. History of any of the following in the 5 years prior to screening: cancer (except thyroid cancer, basal cell skin cancer, or squamous cell skin cancer), skeletal malignancies, bone metastases, irradiation (radiotherapy) to the skeleton, chemotherapy with alkylating agents, Paget disease, fibrous dysplasia, chronic osteomyelitis, bone infarcts, benign bone tumors with curettage and bone grafts, retinoblastoma, or Li-Fraumeni syndrome. Note: Prior systemic radioiodine therapy for thyroid cancer is not exclusionary
4. 4. Presence or history of any disease or condition (eg, drug or alcohol dependence) that, in the view of the investigator, would affect the participant’s safety or places the participant at high risk of poor treatment compliance or of not completing the study.
